instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Script: Gurmukhi. Used in Punjab and Chandigarh, and spoken in Delhi and
Haryana.
Tone: everyday spoken Punjabi.
Words: ਆਨਲਾਈਨ, ਫਾਰਮ, ਪੋਰਟਲ, ਲੌਗਇਨ, ਆਧਾਰ, ਬੈਂਕ, ਮੋਬਾਈਲ, OTP, ਹੈਲਪਲਾਈਨ, ਸਰਟੀਫਿਕੇਟ,
ਡਾਊਨਲੋਡ, ਅਪਲੋਡ.
UI: ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਿਓ, ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰੋ, ਅੱਗੇ, ਪਿੱਛੇ, ਖੋਜੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਸੈਟਿੰਗਾਂ, ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਮਦਦ.
Offices: ਤਹਿਸੀਲਦਾਰ, ਪਟਵਾਰੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ, ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਪੰਚਾਇਤ, ਡਿਪਟੀ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨਰ.
Gender: ਲਿੰਗ. Money: ₹6,000; ₹8 ਲੱਖ. September: ਸਤੰਬਰ.

## Odia (or)

Script: Odia. Used in Odisha.
Tone: everyday spoken Odia.
Words: ଅନଲାଇନ, ଫର୍ମ, ପୋର୍ଟାଲ, ଲଗଇନ, ଆଧାର, ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ, ମୋବାଇଲ, OTP, ହେଲ୍ପଲାଇନ, ସାର୍ଟିଫିକେଟ,
ଡାଉନଲୋଡ, ଅପଲୋଡ.
UI: ଆବେଦନ କରନ୍ତୁ, ଦାଖଲ କରନ୍ତୁ, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ, ପଛକୁ, ଖୋଜନ୍ତୁ, ସେୟାର କରନ୍ତୁ, ସେଟିଂସ୍, ଭାଷା, ସାହାଯ୍ୟ.
Offices: ତହସିଲଦାର, ବିଡିଓ, ଗ୍ରାମ ପଞ୍ଚାୟତ, ଜିଲ୍ଲାପାଳ (କଲେକ୍ଟର), ମୋ ସେବା କେନ୍ଦ୍ର.
Gender: ଲିଙ୍ଗ. Money: ଟ.6,000; ଟ.8 ଲକ୍ଷ. September: ସେପ୍ଟେମ୍ବର.

items.t: The Block Development Office (BDO) in rural areas, the Sub-Divisional Office (SDO), or the ward office in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area. Take your voter ID card (EPIC), Aadhaar and your mobile phone. The form can also be submitted online at socialregistry.wb.gov.in.
Ask at the Block Development Office or the SDO office; check the status and file a grievance on socialregistry.wb.gov.in by logging in with your mobile number and OTP
Department of Women & Child Development and Social Welfare, West Bengal

Money for girls who stay in school and stay unmarried. A girl aged 13 to 18 in Class VIII or above gets a yearly grant (K1), and at 18, if she is still studying and unmarried, a one-time grant (K2), both paid into her own bank account. The scheme was called Kanyashree Prakalpa until 14 August 2026, when the state renamed it Kanyaratna and announced that the yearly grant will double to Rs.2,000 from the 2027 school year and the one-time grant will rise to Rs.50,000; the website, forms and application IDs still say Kanyashree. Girls apply through their school or college, not on their own.
Rs.1,000 a year (Rs.2,000 from 2027) + one-time Rs.25,000 at 18 (Rs.50,000 announced)
Girls aged 13 to 18 for the yearly grant (K1), and 18 to 19 for the one-time grant (K2)

Studying in Class VIII or above in a school, madrasah or open school, or in a college, university or vocational or technical training course. The Class VIII rule is relaxed for girls with 40% or more disability
Her family lives in West Bengal
There is no family income limit (the old Rs.1.2 lakh limit was removed in 2018), and girls who get other scholarships can still apply
Birth certificate issued by the Panchayat or Municipality, copy signed by a parent
Parent's or guardian's declaration that the girl is unmarried (part of the form)
Voter ID card of the parent or legal guardian, self-attested
First page of the bank passbook in the girl's own name, self-attested
Aadhaar card of the girl, if she has one, self-attested
Recent photo of the girl on a white background
Disability certificate, only if she is 13 or older but studying below Class VIII

Her own school, madrasah or college. Ask the Head of the Institution (HOI) or the Kanyashree teacher for the free K1 form (or the K2 form when she turns 18). Hand in the filled form with self-attested copies; the HOI checks it, signs and uploads it on the Kanyashree portal, and gives back the acknowledgement slip with the 20-digit Application ID. If the school does not help, go to the Block Development Officer (village) or Sub-Divisional Officer (town), or the Kanyashree cell in the District Magistrate's office.
The full name of the school or college where she studies now.
In English capital letters, spelt exactly as in her bank passbook, or the money will not reach the account.
As on the birth certificate, in day/month/year.
Tick the class she is studying in this year.
Write both names in full, in capital letters.
Tick the right box for each.
The girl's own Aadhaar number. If she has none yet, leave it blank.
The voter card number of the mother, father or legal guardian.
A number the family always keeps. SMS updates about the application come here.
The account must be in the girl's own name, not a joint or parent's account.
When a girl is 13 and in Class VIII or above, ask the Head of the school for the free K1 form. Open a savings account in her own name first if she has none.
Fill the form in English capital letters, let a parent sign the declaration that she is unmarried, paste the photo and attach the copies.
Hand it in at school. Keep the acknowledgement slip with the 20-digit Application ID.
The block or municipality checks the application and the district sanctions it. The money is sent to her bank account and an SMS comes to the mobile.
Track it on kanyashree.wb.gov.in under Track Application, with the year, the Application ID and her date of birth.
Renew K1 every year through the school until she is 18. If she changes school, the old Head must mark her as transferred on the portal.
When she turns 18, if she is still studying and unmarried, the school applies for the one-time K2 grant by upgrading her old ID.
181 (Women Helpline, also for schoolgirls under Kanyaratna); 033-2337-3846 (Kanyashree portal support, Women & Child Development Department); her school's Head or the Kanyashree cell at the DM office

A one-time grant of Rs.25,000 from the West Bengal government for the first marriage of an adult woman from a poor family. The money goes straight into the bride's own bank account before the wedding date. You fill a free paper form at your block, sub-division or municipal corporation office about one to two months before the wedding; officers then visit your area to check, and the BDO, SDO or Commissioner sanctions it. The new state government kept the scheme in 2026 and added voter-list details to the form.
Rs.25,000 once, into the bride's bank account before the wedding
The bride must be at least 18 and the groom at least 21
It must be her first marriage and she must be unmarried
Family income not more than Rs.1.5 lakh a year
Resident of West Bengal: born in the state, or her parents are permanent residents, or she has lived here for the last 5 years
An active bank account in her name alone, able to receive Rs.25,000 at a time
From 2026: her name, or a parent's or sibling's name, must be in the final voter list, or she must have applied to be enrolled
Filled application form with coloured passport-size photos of the bride and the groom
Bride's age proof, any one: birth certificate, voter ID, Aadhaar, PAN, school leaving certificate or Madhyamik admit card
Groom's age proof, any one of the same documents
Proof of the wedding, any one: invitation card, marriage registration notice, or a self-declaration
Bank passbook page showing her name, account number and IFSC
Copy of her Aadhaar card, with the signed consent on the form
Voter ID (EPIC) details of the bride, or of a parent or sibling, or the acknowledgement number of a new voter enrolment

The Rupashree desk at the Block Development Office if you live in a village, the Sub-Divisional Office if you live in a municipality, or the Municipal Corporation office if you live in a corporation area. Blank forms are free there all year. Hand it in 30 to 60 days before the wedding with self-attested copies, carry the originals for checking, and take the acknowledgement slip with the application number.
In English capital letters, spelt exactly as in your Aadhaar-linked bank account.
As on your age proof. You must be 18 or older.
The wedding date. Apply one to two months before it.
Address of the Venue for the Proposed Wedding Ceremony
Kalitala village, Kalitala GP, Raina-II, Purba Bardhaman, 713421
Where the wedding will take place. Officers may check this during the enquiry.

Your voter details from the final voter list. If your name is not there, give a parent's or sibling's details and tick who it is, or write the acknowledgement number of your new enrolment.
An active account in your name alone. An account not used for months may be blocked and the money will bounce.
Groom's Name in full / Date of Birth
The groom must be at least 21. Attach his age proof.
Tick one: invitation card, marriage registration notice, or self-declaration, and attach it.
One to two months before the wedding, collect the free form from your BDO, SDO or Municipal Corporation office.
Fill it in English capital letters, add your voter details, paste both photos, and sign the declarations and the Aadhaar consent.
Attach the copies and hand it in at the Rupashree desk. Keep the acknowledgement with the application number.
Officers visit your area to check your age, that you are unmarried, the family income, residence and the wedding date.
The BDO, SDO or Commissioner sanctions it, and the Rs.25,000 is sent to your bank account, normally at least 5 days before the wedding date. An SMS comes to your mobile.
You can check the status on rupashree.wb.gov.in under Track Application.
After the wedding, register your marriage with the Marriage Registration Officer; the certificate is needed later for ration card, passport and other papers.
The Rupashree desk at your BDO, SDO or Municipal Corporation office; 033-2337-3846 (Rupashree portal support, Women & Child Development Department); 181 (Women Helpline)
Higher Education Department, Government of West Bengal

An education loan of up to Rs.10 lakh with no collateral and 4% simple interest, for students from West Bengal from Class X up to PhD, studying in the state, elsewhere in India or abroad, or preparing at a coaching centre for medical, engineering, law or UPSC, PSC and SSC exams. Fees are paid straight to the institution and living costs to the student's account. You apply online with a parent or guardian as co-borrower; your institution checks the documents and the bank you choose sanctions the loan and gives the card. The loan is repaid over up to 15 years, starting a year after the course ends or you get a job.
Loan up to Rs.10 lakh at 4% simple interest, no collateral
The student or the family has lived in West Bengal for at least the last 10 years (a self-declaration in the form is enough)
Passed Class IX and studying in Class X, XI or XII, a diploma, UG, PG or PhD, in or outside the state or abroad, or at a coaching centre for entrance or competitive exams
No income limit and no minimum marks
Must apply jointly with a parent, guardian or other co-borrower
No margin money up to Rs.4 lakh; above that, 5%, against which a scholarship such as SVMCM can be counted
Prospectus or certificate from the institution showing admission, exam, hostel and other fees
Marksheet or certificate of the last exam passed
PAN card of the student and of the guardian, or an undertaking if there is none
Address proof of the co-borrower
Colour photos and signatures of the student and the co-borrower (JPG, 20 to 50 KB)
West Bengal Student Credit Card (WBSCC) portal

Mukhya Mantri Swasthya Bima Yojana (MMSBY Card, formerly Swasthya Sathi)
State Health Agency, Health & Family Welfare Department, West Bengal

West Bengal's own health cover for families who had a Swasthya Sathi card but are not on the central Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) list. It gives cashless treatment of up to Rs.5 lakh a year for the whole family at empanelled government and private hospitals, in the state and outside it. Swasthya Sathi is being replaced since Ayushman Bharat started in West Bengal on 16 August 2026: families on the PM-JAY list get the Ayushman card, and the rest move to MMSBY. You check which one is yours with your Aadhaar number on the State Health Agency website, then enrol with your Swasthya Sathi card number.
Up to Rs.5 lakh a year per family, cashless
Your family was enrolled under Swasthya Sathi and you have the 17-character number (URN) printed on the Swasthya Sathi card
Your family is not on the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY list. If it is, you get the Ayushman card instead, not MMSBY
Permanent resident of West Bengal. Families earning more than Rs.8 lakh a year are left out
Not for families covered by WBHS, CGHS, ESI or a PSU or government group medical scheme, or employees and pensioners who get a medical allowance
Members aged 70 and above get the separate Ayushman Vay Vandana card instead
No limit on family size, and illnesses you already have are covered from the first day
Aadhaar card of each family member being enrolled
Swasthya Sathi card, for the 17-character URN number
The mobile number registered with the Swasthya Sathi card, for the OTP
Aadhaar-linked mobile number of each member, for creating the ABHA health ID
Voter ID card (EPIC) of each adult member, with the AC, part and serial number from the voter list
Digital ration card number and its category (RKSY-I or RKSY-II), if you have one
Type any family member's Aadhaar and press Check Status first. The answer tells you whether your family is under PM-JAY or can enrol in MMSBY.
The 17-character number on your Swasthya Sathi smart card. An OTP is sent to the mobile number that was given when the card was made.
District / Block or ULB / Gram Panchayat or Ward

Usually the eldest woman of the family, in whose name the Swasthya Sathi card was made.
For each member card, type that person's Aadhaar and press Validate. Members who are not eligible are struck off automatically.
The category and number printed on your digital ration card. If you choose a category, the ration card number becomes compulsory.
The mobile number linked to this member's Aadhaar. The OTP for the ABHA health ID comes here.
Press Create ABHA ID for every member and enter the OTP. The form will not submit until each eligible member has an ABHA ID.
Copy these from the voter card and the voter list (the AC, part and serial number are shown on the voter slip or the ECI website).
The official or help-desk staff taking your enrolment, for example at a camp or hospital desk, fills in their own details. If you are applying alone and unsure, call 1800-345-5384 before you submit.
Open sha.wbhealth.gov.in, tap Apply for MMSBY, type an Aadhaar number of the family and press Check Status. If it says your family is under PM-JAY, make the Ayushman card instead.
If you can enrol in MMSBY, type the 17-character Swasthya Sathi URN, press Submit URN and enter the OTP sent to the card's registered mobile.
The family details appear already filled in. Check the address, district, block and Gram Panchayat or ward.
For each member, press Validate on the Aadhaar, fill the ration card, mobile, gender, date of birth and voter details, and press Create ABHA ID.
Fill the receiving authority box and press Submit Enrollment. Note down the message shown on the screen.
The health department then does field verification and e-KYC. When the card is activated, you can be treated cashless at any empanelled hospital by showing it at the help desk.
If the hospital asks for money for a covered treatment, or you get stuck, call 1800-345-5384 (24 hours).
